comments.content: Bug: this assigns to `curve2` but the subsequent code and `link1 = subnames1[0]` indicate this branch should populate `curve1`. The original code was `curve1 = Part::Feature::getTopoShape(docobj1, subnames1[0].c_str(), ...)`. As written, `curve1` is now never assigned in this branch and the first `curve2` value is overwritten later, breaking ruled surface creation.

Bug: this now passes `sSubName` instead of `subString.c_str()`. The surrounding logic uses `subString` (e.g. the `strstr(subString.c_str(), "Face")` checks below and the `if (subString.length() > 0)` guard), so passing `sSubName` retrieves the wrong sub-shape. Restore `subString.c_str()`.

Bug: the `simplifyCompound` priority array lists `TopAbs_SHELL` twice and omits `TopAbs_COMPSOLID`... actually COMPSOLID is present, but SHELL appears twice while the original chain was SOLID, COMPSOLID, FACE, SHELL, EDGE, WIRE, VERTEX. Here EDGE is missing (replaced by a duplicate SHELL), so single-edge compounds are no longer simplified. Replace the second `TopAbs_SHELL` with `TopAbs_EDGE`.

This call was changed from `getTopoShape` to `getShape` (returns TopoDS_Shape), then assigned to `TopoShape face = shape;`. Since `getShape` passes `NoElementMap` internally and returns a bare TopoDS_Shape, the element map/hasher is lost compared to the original `getTopoShape` usage. Prefer keeping `getTopoShape` here to preserve element mapping for the subsequent `makeElementFace()`.

Mismatched parentheses in the options expression: the `NeedSubElement` term opens a paren that is never balanced correctly — `(Feature::NeedSubElement * ... | (Feature::Transform * ...) | (Feature::NoElementMap * ...))` wraps Transform and NoElementMap inside the NeedSubElement group. It still evaluates correctly for `|` due to associativity, but the grouping is misleading and error-prone. Recommend removing the stray extra paren after `NeedSubElement * Base::asBoolean(needSubElement)` to match the intended flat OR of four flags.

Operator precedence: `options & Feature::ResolveLink && obj != owner` — `&` has lower precedence than `&&`, so this parses as `options & (Feature::ResolveLink && obj != owner)`, which is not intended. Wrap the flag test in parentheses: `(options & Feature::ResolveLink) && obj != owner`.

Operator precedence: `options & Feature::NeedSubElement && subelement && *subelement` parses as `options & (Feature::NeedSubElement && subelement && *subelement)` because `&&` binds tighter than `&`. Wrap in parentheses: `(options & Feature::NeedSubElement) && subelement && *subelement`.
Operator precedence: `options & NeedSubElement && (...)` binds as `options & (NeedSubElement && (...))`. Wrap the flag test: `(options & NeedSubElement) && (...)`.

Operator precedence: `pmat && options & Transform` parses as `pmat && (options & Transform)` which is actually correct here since `&&` is evaluated after `&`... no—`&` binds tighter than `&&`, so this is fine. However `if (options & Transform)` a few lines above and `(pmat || options & Transform)` in getTopoShape should be double-checked: `pmat || options & Transform` parses as `pmat || (options & Transform)` which is correct. Only flag the `&`/`&&` mixes; verify this line is intended.

Operator precedence: `options & NeedSubElement && !(options & DontSimplifyCompound) && shape.shapeType(true) == TopAbs_COMPOUND` — the leading `options & NeedSubElement` binds incorrectly with `&&`. Parenthesize: `(options & NeedSubElement) && !(options & DontSimplifyCompound) && ...`.
